blocks.html: Addiction is a chronic, relapsing disease of the brain that leads to powerful, often overwhelming urges to use substances despite knowing of the physical, emotional, and behavioral harms caused by their use. Substance use disorders lead to medical and mental health challenges and the loss of millions of lives each year due to overdose or other medical complications. In the last ten years, more than 500,000 Americans of all ages and demographics have died from addiction-related complications.

What to Expect in a Frisco, TX Drug Rehab

blocks.html: When choosing a Frisco, TX drug rehab, you should expect a treatment program designed around your specific treatment needs and goals. Although millions of people suffer from the physical and emotional challenges of addiction, no two people experience addiction in the same way. Several individual factors will directly influence what your journey to sobriety looks like. Because of the unique nature of addiction, choosing a rehab that develops its addiction treatment programs based on your individual needs rather than the substance you are looking to quit is crucial.

blocks.html: If you have an addiction to opioids, alcohol, or benzodiazepines. In that case, selecting a treatment program that provides medically assisted detox services is crucial to ensuring you receive the vital support and safety monitoring you may need throughout detox and withdrawal. Unfortunately, detoxing from certain drugs, such as the ones listed above, is often complicated and can result in dangerous and sometimes life-threatening withdrawal symptoms for some. In a medically-supervised detox program, medical and mental health providers provide support and care throughout the stages of detox. This may include interventions like monitoring your physical health (vital signs, etc.) and administering medications to help reduce the intensity and severity of specific withdrawal symptoms.

blocks.html: You can also expect medical and mental health providers skilled in treating dual diagnosis conditions. A dual diagnosis occurs when someone simultaneously experiences the symptoms of a substance use disorder and a mental health condition. These circumstances arise with far more frequency than many realize. Some studies suggest up to half of those who seek help to overcome addiction, or a mental health challenge have a dual diagnosis. Research shows dual diagnosis symptoms are highly intertwined, and treating one without addressing the other is challenging and not beneficial for the person seeking treatment.
